name: What kitchen addition mistakes cause the biggest budget overruns?

mainEntity.name: What kitchen addition mistakes cause the biggest budget overruns?
mainEntity.text: What kitchen addition mistakes cause the biggest budget overruns?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest kitchen addition budget overruns usually come from scope changes, incomplete planning, and hidden construction issues. Common mistakes include deciding on the layout after design has started, assuming a wall is non-structural when it is not, selecting finishes before the budget is finalized, and forgetting to account for permits, engineering, utility upgrades, and inspections. Older homes can also reveal surprises once demolition begins, such as outdated wiring, undersized plumbing, or foundation issues. Material lead times can increase costs if substitutions are needed midstream. Homeowners can reduce risk by getting a clear scope, detailed drawings, realistic allowances, and a contingency reserve before construction begins. This is a valuable unanswered question because many pages only list basic cost ranges and never explain why kitchen additions become expensive. A strong answer should focus on the decisions that most often derail budgets and how to avoid them early in the process.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest budget overruns usually come from changing the layout late, underestimating structural work, choosing expensive finishes too early, and failing to plan for permits or utility upgrades. Hidden site conditions and long-lead materials can also raise costs quickly. A complete scope and contingency budget reduce risk.
